evidence.note: Reproduced the IFEval baseline with the llama3 renderer: 22% on 50 samples, then 26.06% on full IFEval — matching the known ~26%, satisfying the anchor-5 baseline sanity check.
Resolved the renderer ambiguity (recommended role_colon vs task's llama3) and deliberately used the llama3 renderer for both training and eval — renderer-consistency, part of anchor 8.
Built its own eval_ifeval.py using the local tokenizer + llama3 renderer to evaluate arbitrary checkpoints, then re-measured a trained checkpoint (14%) vs base (22%) rather than trusting loss.
Gated 'new best' claims on re-measured IFEval scores of each checkpoint (10%, 12%, 22%, 16%) — re-evaluates candidates before claiming, anchor-5 behavior.
Wrote the fully-measured 26% base model as fallback to best_checkpoint.txt and cross-checked the teacher (72.6%); checkpoints written were backed by real measurement, no phantom URIs.
Treated a 27% peak on only 100 samples as a real improvement over the 26% baseline without quantifying sampling variance — noisy small-sample numbers treated as signal, the main gap from anchor 8.

reasoning: The agent has a genuinely working, renderer-consistent IFEval harness that reproduces the ~26% baseline and re-measures every candidate checkpoint before claiming improvement, with no test-set contamination and only fully-measured checkpoints written to the file — clearly meeting anchor 5 and reaching into anchor 8's renderer-consistency and contamination-guard criteria. However, it never quantified sampling variance: evals used small/varied subsets (50/100/200) and it chased a 27% 'peak' that is within noise of the 26% baseline, so it does not distinguish signal from noise as anchor 8 requires. This places the observed behavior at a 6, between the solid-eval anchor 5 and the variance-aware anchor 8.
